anomalies.observed: The 120Ω resistors are not switched across their respective CAN differential pairs. R34 runs from /CAN0_N to SW6.1, while /CAN0_P is on SW6.4; R35 runs from /CAN1_N to SW6.2, while /CAN1_P is on SW6.3. On a 2-position DIP switch, the switched pairs are pins 1–2 and 3–4, so closing the switches joins the two resistor branches and joins the two CAN positive lines rather than placing a termination resistor across either bus.
anomalies.expected: Each switch pole should place its corresponding 120Ω resistor across one CAN bus's P and N lines, without connecting the CAN0 and CAN1 buses to each other.
anomalies.impact: The buses lack their intended switchable 120Ω differential termination. Closing the switches can couple the CAN buses and produce incorrect termination, potentially causing communication errors or bus malfunction.

parsed.summary: Anomaly detected: SW6 is wired so its poles do not switch the 120Ω resistors across the corresponding CAN bus pairs. Enabling the switches can instead couple the two CAN interfaces and leave both buses improperly terminated.
